science_card_focus: Revise the same incompressible-energy scaling ScienceCard against the frozen source. Preserve every already source-supported field, close every review issue exactly, include the complete reported fit-parameter uncertainties and all needed unit/domain/operational-definition locators, and omit nonessential fast-quench discussion unless fully source-located.

issues.detail: The parameter and claim uncertainty fields now retain +/-5.010e4, +/-0.052, +/-2.951e4, and +/-0.068 correctly, and oracle_outputs correctly remain central-only. However, both quantitative_form strings still omit those source-reported plus/minus values, contrary to the prior repair request and extraction contract. Render the two quantitative forms with the reported amplitude and exponent uncertainties. Also remove fit_uncertainty_convention from source_ambiguities: its own statement correctly says this is missing metadata, not a contradiction, so it must remain only as source_unspecified uncertainty provenance.

Both applicability strings still assert that tau_Q<=10 may deviate because KZM breaks down, but neither claim includes the source locator at line 345. Apply the previous minimal repair by deleting this out-of-domain aside, or add line 345 to each claim and state that it is a general KZM/spectral-collapse limitation rather than support for the E_i fitted domain. The [100,1000] fitted-curve domain itself remains correctly anchored at lines 1110-1112.

temperature_lowT, temperature_T1, and the E_i readout each assert dimensionless scaled units, but their own anchor lists do not include the source's dimensionless/scaled-unit definition. Add line 148 or line 460 to those records, or remove the unit qualifier from branch-condition statements where the schema does not require it. The common simulation condition now anchors line 460 correctly; that does not by itself satisfy the per-record factual-anchor requirement.

previous_science_card.assessment: The source supports the incompressible kinetic energy E_i scaling with quench duration tau_Q at two temperatures (T=10^-6 and T=1), with fitted power laws and explicit fit uncertainties. The operational definition of equilibration time is provided in the supplementary material. The control tau_Q is a linear chemical-potential ramp with dimensionless scaled units. The readout E_i is defined via the density-weighted velocity field and its incompressible component. The claims are anchored to the relevant lines, including the fit method and ensemble counts. The applicability domain [100,1000] is supported by reviewer figure evidence and the source's own fit ranges. The fast-quench deviation statement is noted as a general limitation, not part of the fitted domain. The paper scope is revised to avoid conflating scaling with collapse. The fit uncertainty convention is source_unspecified, and the numeric values are preserved. The card is case_authoring_ready true.

mechanisms.statement: The incompressible kinetic energy at equilibration scales as E_i proportional to tau_Q^{-(1+2 nu)/(1+z nu)}, with mean-field exponents nu=1/2 and z=2, giving E_i proportional to tau_Q^{-1}.

previous_science_card.paper_scope: The paper establishes the Kibble-Zurek universality of the total incompressible kinetic energy E_i at equilibration time, reporting fitted power-law scalings with quench duration tau_Q at two temperatures (T=10^-6 and T=1). The separate collapse of rescaled spectra is not part of this selected cluster.

anchors.support: Density-weighted velocity field u = |Psi_C| v, decomposition into compressible and incompressible components, and definition of E_i,c = (1/2) integral |u_i,c|^2 d^2r.
E_i defined as (1/2) integral |u_i(r, t_eq)|^2 d^2r = integral_0^infinity E_i(k) dk.
Each data point is averaged over (a) R=2000 and (b) R=1000 stochastic realizations. Error bars denote 1 standard deviation.

readouts.definition: Total incompressible kinetic energy at equilibration time, defined as E_i = (1/2) integral |u_i(r, t_eq)|^2 d^2r = integral_0^infinity E_i(k) dk, where u_i is the incompressible (solenoidal) component of the density-weighted velocity field u = |Psi_C| v.
readouts.name: E_i
readouts.statistic: Ensemble average over R=2000 (T=10^-6) and R=1000 (T=1) stochastic realizations.
